easy: Likely to do something, often something bad.

ex.en: Glass is liable to break if you drop it.
ex.ko: 유리는 떨어뜨리면 깨지기 쉽다.

easy: Responsible by law, so you might have to pay or get in trouble.

ex.en: You are liable if you break your neighbor's window.
ex.ko: 이웃집 창문을 깨면 네가 책임을 져야 한다.

easy: The middle of a group or crowd of things.

ex.en: The puppy sat in the midst of the toys.
ex.ko: 강아지는 장난감들 한가운데에 앉아 있었다.

easy: A very hard and sad way of living, with lots of trouble.

ex.en: The family lived in misery after the storm destroyed their home.
ex.ko: 폭풍이 집을 망가뜨린 뒤 그 가족은 비참하게 살았다.

easy: A very big feeling of sadness.

ex.en: I felt pure misery when my pet fish died.
ex.ko: 내 물고기가 죽었을 때 나는 정말 괴로웠다.

easy: A part of a spaceship that can be taken off and used on its own.

ex.en: The astronauts climbed into the module to land on the moon.
ex.ko: 우주비행사들은 달에 착륙하려고 모듈에 올라탔다.

easy: A building where Muslim people pray.

ex.en: My friend goes to the mosque with his family every Friday.
ex.ko: 내 친구는 매주 금요일 가족과 함께 모스크에 간다.

easy: The best and most important player on a team.

ex.en: Our pitcher was named MVP of the season.
ex.ko: 우리 투수가 이번 시즌 최우수 선수로 뽑혔다.

easy: A room in a house just for a baby.

ex.en: The baby fell asleep in the nursery.
ex.ko: 아기는 아기방에서 잠이 들었다.

easy: The round part of a plant that we eat; it makes your eyes water.

ex.en: Dad cut an onion and it made me cry.
ex.ko: 아빠가 양파를 썰자 나는 눈물이 났다.

easy: A plant with a round bulb that grows under the ground and is used in cooking.

ex.en: Mom planted an onion in our garden.
ex.ko: 엄마는 우리 정원에 양파를 심었다.

easy: A sickness that spreads fast and makes many people very sick.

ex.en: Long ago, a plague spread through the town.
ex.ko: 옛날에 그 마을에 전염병이 퍼졌다.

easy: Really and completely; it makes a word stronger.

ex.en: The ice cream was positively delicious.
ex.ko: 그 아이스크림은 정말 맛있었다.

easy: In a good and hopeful way.

ex.en: Think positively before the big test.
ex.ko: 큰 시험 전에는 긍정적으로 생각해 봐.

easy: Being chased by someone who wants to catch or hurt it.

ex.en: The pursued rabbit ran into its hole.
ex.ko: 쫓기던 토끼는 굴속으로 달려 들어갔다.

easy: The one who is being chased.

ex.en: In tag, the pursued runs away from the catcher.
ex.ko: 술래잡기에서 쫓기는 사람은 술래에게서 도망간다.

easy: To ask people to join a team or job.

ex.en: Our coach recruited new players for the soccer team.
ex.ko: 우리 코치님은 축구팀에 들어올 새 선수들을 모집했다.

easy: A tricky person who is not honest.

ex.en: The rogue tricked people into giving him money.
ex.ko: 그 사기꾼은 사람들을 속여 돈을 받아 갔다.

easy: Sitting down on a chair or the floor.

ex.en: The seated children listened to the story.
ex.ko: 앉아 있는 아이들은 이야기를 들었다.

easy: In an angry, harsh way.

ex.en: The teacher spoke sharply when we ran in the hall.
ex.ko: 우리가 복도에서 뛰자 선생님은 날카롭게 말씀하셨다.

easy: In a clear way, with edges that are easy to see.

ex.en: The mountains stood out sharply against the sky.
ex.ko: 산들이 하늘을 배경으로 선명하게 드러났다.

easy: A word you write at the end of a letter, before your name.

ex.en: I wrote "Sincerely, Mina" at the end of my letter.
ex.ko: 나는 편지 끝에 "진심을 담아, 미나"라고 썼다.

easy: When people stand together and help each other.

ex.en: The class showed solidarity by helping the new student.
ex.ko: 반 친구들은 새로 온 학생을 도우며 하나로 뭉쳤다.

easy: The thing that someone does best.

ex.en: Baking cookies is my sister's specialty.
ex.ko: 쿠키 굽기는 우리 언니의 특기다.

easy: Magical; something science cannot explain, like ghosts.

ex.en: Ghosts are supernatural beings in my storybook.
ex.ko: 내 동화책에서 유령은 초자연적인 존재이다.

easy: Magic things like ghosts that science cannot explain.

ex.en: My brother loves stories about the supernatural.
ex.ko: 내 동생은 초자연적인 것에 대한 이야기를 좋아한다.

easy: One more than twelve.

ex.en: Thirteen kids came to my party.
ex.ko: 열세 명의 아이들이 내 생일 파티에 왔다.

easy: The number that comes after twelve.

ex.en: Seven plus six makes thirteen.
ex.ko: 7 더하기 6은 13이다.

easy: A special thing that makes someone or something easy to know.

ex.en: A big smile is her trademark.
ex.ko: 활짝 웃는 미소가 그녀의 트레이드마크다.

easy: A name or sign that a company owns and puts on its products.

ex.en: The shoe has the company's trademark on the side.
ex.ko: 그 신발 옆면에는 회사의 상표가 붙어 있다.

easy: To cut off the edges to make something smaller or neat.

ex.en: Mom helped me trim my fingernails.
ex.ko: 엄마는 내 손톱 다듬는 것을 도와주셨다.

easy: To decorate something with pretty things.

ex.en: We trimmed the tree with lights and ornaments.
ex.ko: 우리는 나무를 전구와 장식품으로 꾸몄다.

easy: A thing you hold over your head to keep dry in the rain.

ex.en: I opened my umbrella when it began to rain.
ex.ko: 비가 오기 시작하자 나는 우산을 폈다.

easy: A big church where monks or nuns live and pray.

ex.en: We visited an old abbey on our trip to England.
ex.ko: 우리는 영국 여행에서 오래된 수도원을 방문했다.

easy: A home for nuns, led by a woman called the abbess.

ex.en: The nuns in the abbey grew vegetables in the garden.
ex.ko: 수녀원의 수녀님들은 정원에서 채소를 길렀다.

easy: A small change to make something fit better.

ex.en: Mom made an adjustment to my pants so they fit.
ex.ko: 엄마가 내 바지를 조금 고쳐서 몸에 맞게 해 주셨다.

easy: A warm feeling of love for someone or something.

ex.en: My little brother has a strong attachment to his blanket.
ex.ko: 내 동생은 자기 담요에 강한 애착을 갖고 있다.

easy: An extra part you can add to a tool or machine.

ex.en: The vacuum has a long attachment for the corners.
ex.ko: 그 청소기에는 구석을 청소하는 긴 부속품이 있다.

easy: A small, soft rabbit.

ex.en: The bunny hopped across the yard and ate a carrot.
ex.ko: 토끼가 마당을 깡충깡충 건너가 당근을 먹었다.

easy: A stick of wax with a string in the middle that burns to give light.

ex.en: We blew out the candles on my birthday cake.
ex.ko: 우리는 내 생일 케이크의 양초를 불어서 껐다.

easy: Made by cutting a shape into wood or stone.

ex.en: The carved wooden box had a bird on the lid.
ex.ko: 조각된 나무 상자 뚜껑에는 새가 새겨져 있었다.

easy: A group of people who sing together, often in church.

ex.en: My sister sings in the school choir.
ex.ko: 우리 언니는 학교 합창단에서 노래한다.

easy: The white food inside a coconut.

ex.en: The cake had sweet coconut on top.
ex.ko: 케이크 위에 달콤한 코코넛이 올려져 있었다.

easy: A big, hard, round fruit with white food and juice inside.

ex.en: We drank juice from a coconut on the beach.
ex.ko: 우리는 해변에서 코코넛 주스를 마셨다.

easy: Telling that you did something wrong.

ex.en: Ben made a confession: he ate the last cookie.
ex.ko: 벤은 마지막 쿠키를 먹었다고 고백했다.

easy: To eat or drink all of something quickly.

ex.en: The hungry boys consumed a whole pizza in minutes.
ex.ko: 배고픈 소년들은 몇 분 만에 피자 한 판을 다 먹어 치웠다.

easy: To eat or drink something.

ex.en: Try not to consume too much candy.
ex.ko: 사탕을 너무 많이 먹지 않도록 해 봐.

easy: How much people can believe and trust you.

ex.en: Telling the truth gives you credibility with your friends.
ex.ko: 진실을 말하면 친구들에게 신뢰를 얻는다.

easy: In a way that looks carefully at the good and bad parts.

ex.en: Read the story critically and ask if it makes sense.
ex.ko: 그 이야기를 비판적으로 읽고 말이 되는지 생각해 봐.

easy: Not able to pay attention because you are worried.

ex.en: Tom was distracted and worried about his lost dog.
ex.ko: 톰은 잃어버린 개 걱정에 정신이 딴 데 팔려 있었다.

easy: A unit of length that is one tenth of a meter.

ex.en: My pencil is about 2 dm long.
ex.ko: 내 연필은 길이가 약 2dm이다.

easy: One more than thirteen.

ex.en: Fourteen kids came to my party.
ex.ko: 열네 명의 아이들이 내 파티에 왔다.

easy: The number that comes after thirteen.

ex.en: Seven times two is fourteen.
ex.ko: 7 곱하기 2는 14이다.

easy: A kind of math about shapes, lines, and angles.

ex.en: In geometry class, we drew triangles and circles.
ex.ko: 기하학 시간에 우리는 삼각형과 원을 그렸다.

easy: A doctor who treats all kinds of illnesses.

ex.en: I saw my GP when I had a bad cough.
ex.ko: 나는 기침이 심해서 일반의를 찾아갔다.

easy: The act of pulling something heavy.

ex.en: The haul of the sled up the hill made us tired.
ex.ko: 썰매를 언덕 위로 끌고 가는 일은 우리를 지치게 했다.

easy: The amount of fish or other things you catch or get.

ex.en: Dad's haul of fish filled two buckets.
ex.ko: 아빠가 잡은 물고기는 양동이 두 개를 가득 채웠다.

easy: A line of words at the top that tells what is below.

ex.en: The header on my essay says "My Pet Dog."
ex.ko: 내 글의 제목은 "나의 반려견"이다.

easy: A bush with shiny, prickly leaves and red berries.

ex.en: We put holly on the door at Christmas.
ex.ko: 우리는 크리스마스에 문에 호랑가시나무를 걸어 두었다.

easy: To get in the way and make something hard to do.

ex.en: Loud music interferes with my homework.
ex.ko: 시끄러운 음악이 내 숙제를 방해한다.

easy: To step in to stop or change what is happening.

ex.en: Please don't interfere when my brother and I play.
ex.ko: 남동생과 내가 놀 때 끼어들지 마.

easy: The spot where two lines cross.

ex.en: The two lines meet at an intersection on the graph.
ex.ko: 두 선은 그래프에서 한 교차점에서 만난다.

easy: A place where two roads cross.

ex.en: Look both ways at the intersection before you cross.
ex.ko: 교차로에서는 건너기 전에 양쪽을 살펴봐.

easy: The sound of hitting a door to ask to come in.

ex.en: The knocking on the door woke the dog.
ex.ko: 문 두드리는 소리에 개가 깼다.

easy: A piece of cloth sewn on the inside of a coat.

ex.en: My winter coat has a warm lining.
ex.ko: 내 겨울 코트에는 따뜻한 안감이 있다.

easy: Making a map of a place.

ex.en: Mapping the island took the scientists a week.
ex.ko: 그 섬의 지도를 만드는 데 과학자들은 일주일이 걸렸다.

easy: A measuring unit like the meter, gram, or liter.

ex.en: We learned that a gram is a metric unit.
ex.ko: 우리는 그램이 미터법 단위라는 것을 배웠다.

easy: Saying the name of things.

ex.en: Naming all fifty states was hard for me.
ex.ko: 50개 주 이름을 모두 말하는 것은 나에게 어려웠다.

easy: Being close to something.

ex.en: We live in close proximity to the park.
ex.ko: 우리는 공원 바로 가까이에 산다.

easy: The area close around a person or thing.

ex.en: No dogs are allowed in the proximity of the pool.
ex.ko: 수영장 근처에는 개가 들어올 수 없다.

easy: A person who takes care of a forest or park.

ex.en: The ranger taught us how to put out a campfire.
ex.ko: 공원 관리원은 캠프파이어 끄는 법을 알려 주셨다.

easy: Turned the other way around, in the opposite order.

ex.en: The letters in my name were reversed on the paper.
ex.ko: 내 이름의 글자가 종이에 거꾸로 되어 있었다.

easy: The feeling you have when you are not happy.

ex.en: I felt sadness when my best friend moved away.
ex.ko: 가장 친한 친구가 이사 갔을 때 나는 슬펐다.

easy: Feeling unhappy and heavy in your heart.

ex.en: Tears of sadness ran down her face.
ex.ko: 슬픔의 눈물이 그녀의 얼굴에 흘러내렸다.

easy: Choosing carefully only the best ones.

ex.en: I am selective about which books I read.
ex.ko: 나는 읽을 책을 신중하게 고른다.

easy: Very careful and picky about what to choose.

ex.en: The cat is very selective about its food.
ex.ko: 그 고양이는 먹이에 매우 까다롭다.

easy: Smooth and bright, so it shines in the light.

ex.en: She polished the table until it was shiny.
ex.ko: 그녀는 탁자가 반짝일 때까지 닦았다.

easy: Smelling bad, like old milk.

ex.en: The milk smelled sour, so we threw it away.
ex.ko: 우유에서 시큼한 냄새가 나서 우리는 그것을 버렸다.

easy: Having a sharp taste, like a lemon.

ex.en: The lemon was so sour that my face scrunched up.
ex.ko: 레몬이 너무 셔서 내 얼굴이 찡그려졌다.

easy: A tool with a small bowl and a handle, used to eat soup or cereal.

ex.en: I ate my cereal with a big spoon.
ex.ko: 나는 큰 숟가락으로 시리얼을 먹었다.

easy: As much as one spoon can hold.

ex.en: Add two spoons of sugar to the tea.
ex.ko: 차에 설탕을 두 숟가락 넣어.

easy: Loosened and not stiff after stretching.

ex.en: My stretched legs felt ready to run.
ex.ko: 스트레칭으로 풀린 내 다리는 달릴 준비가 되어 있었다.

easy: Spread out over a big area.

ex.en: The beach lay stretched out in front of us.
ex.ko: 해변이 우리 앞에 쭉 펼쳐져 있었다.

easy: The act of pulling something in with your mouth.

ex.en: Sucking juice through a straw is fun.
ex.ko: 빨대로 주스를 빨아 마시는 것은 재미있다.

easy: A soft toy bear that kids hug.

ex.en: I hug my teddy when I go to bed.
ex.ko: 나는 잠자리에 들 때 곰 인형을 안는다.

easy: A flat outdoor area next to a house, where people sit.

ex.en: We ate lunch on the terrace in the sun.
ex.ko: 우리는 햇볕이 드는 테라스에서 점심을 먹었다.

easy: A person who steals things.

ex.en: A police officer caught the thief who stole the bike.
ex.ko: 경찰관이 자전거를 훔친 도둑을 잡았다.

easy: Without any doubt; for sure.

ex.en: Our dog is undoubtedly the cutest in town.
ex.ko: 우리 개는 틀림없이 동네에서 가장 귀엽다.

easy: To make a high sound by blowing air through your lips.

ex.en: Dad whistles a happy song while he cooks.
ex.ko: 아빠는 요리하면서 즐거운 노래를 휘파람으로 부신다.

easy: To move fast with a high sound.

ex.en: The ball whistled past my ear.
ex.ko: 공이 내 귀 옆을 쌩 하고 지나갔다.

easy: Using mean and hurtful words.

ex.en: Calling people names is abusive and wrong.
ex.ko: 남에게 욕을 하는 것은 모욕적이고 잘못된 일이다.

easy: A strong wish for something, like food.

ex.en: Playing outside gave me a big appetite.
ex.ko: 밖에서 놀았더니 식욕이 왕성해졌다.

easy: The grass area behind a house.

ex.en: We played catch in the backyard.
ex.ko: 우리는 뒤뜰에서 캐치볼을 했다.

easy: A very big sign outside, by the road, with an ad on it.

ex.en: We saw a huge billboard for ice cream on the highway.
ex.ko: 우리는 고속도로에서 아이스크림 광고판을 크게 보았다.

easy: A mean person who hurts or scares others.

ex.en: A bully took Sam's lunch, so he told the teacher.
ex.ko: 괴롭히는 아이가 샘의 점심을 빼앗아서 샘은 선생님께 말했다.

easy: To ask someone for advice.

ex.en: I consulted my teacher about my science project.
ex.ko: 나는 과학 프로젝트에 대해 선생님과 의논했다.

easy: To look in a book to find information.

ex.en: Consult a dictionary when you find a new word.
ex.ko: 새 단어를 만나면 사전을 찾아봐.

easy: Mixed into a liquid so you cannot see it anymore.

ex.en: The dissolved sugar disappeared in the hot tea.
ex.ko: 녹은 설탕은 뜨거운 차 속에서 보이지 않게 되었다.

easy: To be the biggest or strongest part of something.

ex.en: Tall trees dominate the forest.
ex.ko: 그 숲에서는 키 큰 나무가 가장 많다.

easy: To be in charge and control others.

ex.en: A bossy player can dominate the whole game.
ex.ko: 잘난 척하는 선수는 경기 전체를 쥐락펴락할 수 있다.

easy: An expert who studies money, jobs, and how things are sold.

ex.en: An economist explained why prices go up.
ex.ko: 경제학자가 물가가 오르는 이유를 설명해 주었다.

easy: In many places or in a big way.

ex.en: This book is used extensively in schools.
ex.ko: 이 책은 학교에서 널리 쓰인다.

easy: A US group that checks that food and medicine are safe.

ex.en: The FDA checks that our food is safe to eat.
ex.ko: 식품의약국은 우리가 먹는 음식이 안전한지 검사한다.

easy: The part of your face above your eyes.

ex.en: Mom felt my forehead to see if I had a fever.
ex.ko: 엄마는 내가 열이 있는지 내 이마를 짚어 보셨다.

easy: A kind feeling that lets you stop being angry at someone.

ex.en: She asked for forgiveness after she broke my toy.
ex.ko: 그녀는 내 장난감을 망가뜨린 뒤 용서를 구했다.

easy: When you say it is okay and stop being angry about a mistake.

ex.en: Tom gave her forgiveness and they played again.
ex.ko: 톰은 그녀를 용서했고 그들은 다시 함께 놀았다.

easy: A narrow valley, often with a stream.

ex.en: A little stream ran through the glen.
ex.ko: 작은 시냇물이 골짜기를 따라 흘렀다.

easy: A low plant with tiny purple flowers that grows on hills.

ex.en: Purple heather covered the hills of Scotland.
ex.ko: 보라색 히스가 스코틀랜드의 언덕을 뒤덮었다.

easy: In a way that breaks the law.

ex.en: Cars that park illegally can get a ticket.
ex.ko: 불법 주차를 한 차는 딱지를 받을 수 있다.

easy: Liking or likely to do something.

ex.en: I am inclined to stay home when it rains.
ex.ko: 나는 비가 오면 집에 있고 싶어진다.

easy: Slanted, not flat or straight up.

ex.en: We rolled the ball down the inclined board.
ex.ko: 우리는 경사진 판자 아래로 공을 굴렸다.

easy: Relaxed, not fancy or strict.

ex.en: Our class party was informal, so we wore jeans.
ex.ko: 우리 반 파티는 격식이 없어서 청바지를 입었다.

easy: Not official, with no strict rules or papers.

ex.en: We made an informal deal to share the swing.
ex.ko: 우리는 그네를 같이 타기로 비공식적으로 약속했다.

easy: Giving something to someone for a while to get it back later.

ex.en: The library offers free lending of books.
ex.ko: 도서관은 책을 무료로 빌려준다.

easy: An object that shows where something is.

ex.en: A red flag was the marker for the finish line.
ex.ko: 빨간 깃발이 결승선의 표지였다.

easy: The time of life when you are a grown-up.

ex.en: A puppy reaches maturity in about a year.
ex.ko: 강아지는 약 1년이면 다 자란다.

easy: Being fully grown, or acting wise like an adult.

ex.en: Sam showed maturity when he said sorry first.
ex.ko: 샘은 먼저 사과하며 성숙한 모습을 보였다.

easy: A person from an old people of Mexico and Central America.

ex.en: The Maya built tall stone pyramids.
ex.ko: 마야 사람들은 높은 돌 피라미드를 지었다.

easy: Dirty and not neat.

ex.en: My messy room has socks all over the floor.
ex.ko: 내 지저분한 방은 바닥에 양말이 널려 있다.

easy: A secret fighter from old Japan who moved very quietly.

ex.en: The ninja in the movie jumped onto the roof.
ex.ko: 영화 속 닌자는 지붕 위로 뛰어올랐다.

easy: A bird that hunts at night and has big eyes.

ex.en: An owl hooted from the tree at night.
ex.ko: 올빼미가 밤에 나무에서 울었다.

easy: A store where you buy medicine.

ex.en: Mom picked up my medicine at the pharmacy.
ex.ko: 엄마는 약국에서 내 약을 받아 오셨다.

easy: Not sure, and likely to cause trouble.

ex.en: It is problematic to plan a picnic when it may rain.
ex.ko: 비가 올 수도 있는데 소풍을 계획하는 것은 불확실하다.

easy: Used to tell people about something and get them to buy it.

ex.en: The store gave out promotional stickers.
ex.ko: 그 가게는 홍보용 스티커를 나눠 주었다.

easy: Likely to happen or become something in the future.

ex.en: The school held a tour for prospective students.
ex.ko: 학교는 입학할 예비 학생들을 위한 견학을 열었다.

easy: To control or adjust something to keep it right.

ex.en: A thermostat regulates the heat in our house.
ex.ko: 온도 조절기가 우리 집의 온도를 조절한다.

easy: To make rules that control what people do.

ex.en: Laws regulate how fast cars can go.
ex.ko: 법은 자동차가 얼마나 빨리 달릴 수 있는지 규제한다.

easy: A large piece of meat cooked in the oven.

ex.en: Grandma cooked a big roast for Sunday dinner.
ex.ko: 할머니는 일요일 저녁으로 큰 구운 고기를 요리하셨다.

easy: A shop where people get haircuts.

ex.en: Mom got her hair cut at the salon.
ex.ko: 엄마는 미용실에서 머리를 자르셨다.

easy: One more than sixteen.

ex.en: My big sister is seventeen years old.
ex.ko: 우리 언니는 열일곱 살이다.

easy: The number that comes after sixteen.

ex.en: Nine plus eight is seventeen.
ex.ko: 9 더하기 8은 17이다.

easy: To move food or drink down your throat.

ex.en: Chew your food well before you swallow.
ex.ko: 삼키기 전에 음식을 잘 씹어라.

easy: Done in a careful way, step by step, in order.

ex.en: We did a systematic search of the room, one corner at a time.
ex.ko: 우리는 한 구석씩 차례로 방을 체계적으로 뒤졌다.

easy: Not good enough.

ex.en: My coach said losing without trying is unacceptable.
ex.ko: 코치님은 노력도 안 하고 지는 것은 받아들일 수 없다고 하셨다.

easy: Not allowed or welcome.

ex.en: Hitting other kids is unacceptable at school.
ex.ko: 학교에서 다른 아이를 때리는 것은 용납할 수 없다.

easy: Not knowing about something.

ex.en: Leo was unaware that his shoe was untied.
ex.ko: 레오는 신발끈이 풀린 것을 알지 못했다.

easy: Not often seen or found.

ex.en: Snow is uncommon in Florida.
ex.ko: 플로리다에서는 눈이 흔하지 않다.

easy: Special and hard to find.

ex.en: A four-leaf clover is an uncommon find.
ex.ko: 네잎클로버는 보기 드문 발견이다.
